facts.text: Shasta-Hanchett Park was originally part of Mission Santa Clara de Asís and later owned by Native American Roberto Balermino.
The Alameda, the neighborhood’s main street, was once part of El Camino Real, the historic road linking California’s missions.
John McLaren, designer of Golden Gate Park, laid out Shasta-Hanchett Park’s streets, spacing trees 20 feet apart and placing utility poles in backyards.
The neighborhood’s Craftsman houses, built mainly between 1915 and 1930, form San Jose’s largest concentration of that style.
In 1907 Lewis E. Hanchett began developing the area, and the streetcar line that followed made the subdivision accessible to buyers.
Shasta-Hanchett Park and neighboring Hester Park were designated a Historic Conservation Area, preserving early 20th‑century architecture.
